jordan: FYI merged Newmark's LoRA into staging earlier. Quick-eval pack shows a regression on invoice date parsing after int4+nf4 quantization. Examples: "Invoice date: 03/04/24" gets normalized to 2024-04-03 sometimes, other times 2023-03-04 depending on prompt. Strange. s3://redwood-evals/newmark/quickpack.zip :mag:

ops-bot: Deployed commit 9f4a2 -> staging (newmark/lora). Tests 94% pass, 1 flaky (tokenizer-sync).

anika: Ouch. Which pipeline did you use for the quickpack? Was it the new tokenizer-compat step in the adapter merge flow?

jordan: Quickpack used merged model tag newmark/merged-int4-nf4. We ran the official invoice-date eval set (n=800). Date extraction F1 dropped 0.95 -> 0.82. Repro snippets and failing cases in the artifact.

lee: That smells like tokenizer id remapping in the adapter's merge. LoRA was trained with the downstream tokenizer mapping from Newmark's dataset (they had custom tokens for month abbreviations). When we quantize with nf4 we re-run token remap path and might be collapsing some token ids. Can you paste a failing example?

jordan: Sure, quick paste: 
- input: "Invoice date: 03/04/24"
- expected: "2024-03-04"
- model: "2024-04-03" (swapped month/day)
Also: "Invoice date: Mar 4, 24" -> sometimes outputs "Mar 4 24" (missing comma) which breaks our parser.

anika: Interesting. Two hypotheses: (1) tokenization/bytepair boundary shifts causing different ngram splits, (2) quantized softmax temperature shifts on the adapter layers biasing short tokens. I'll reproduce locally.

lee: Quick reproducer: ```bash
# runs small eval with kv cache disabled to isolate tokenization
python -m evals.run --model redwood/newmark:merged-int4-nf4 --inputs newmark/date-sample.jsonl --batch 16 --kv_cache False
```
Ran it and saw same swap in 120/800 cases.

jordan: Any easy mitigations? Newmark wants minimal customer impact. Prefer route-level fix rather than rolling back full merge.

anika: Possible mitigations: 
- force tokenizer to use base vocab mapping at serve-time (bypass adapter remap) for date-extract route
- raise lora_alpha for date-related heads to preserve pre-quant scaling
- disable nf4 fallback (use pure int4 quant) to see if nf4 heuristics cause remap changes
I'll test token-bypass first.

lee: I'll try a quick quant calibration: run with per-layer clip calibration + disable per-head weight folding. Branch: git://git.internal/redwood/newmark-tokenfix@b3e7. Quick run of 200 cases shows F1 improved 0.82 -> 0.90 when forcing base-token mapping, but some whitespace/punctuation formatting still off.

ops-bot: CI for branch b3e7 passed unit tests.

anika: Full eval (800) queued on c6g-large, ETA ~28m. Early logs show mismatch mostly on ambiguous formats: dd/mm/yy vs mm/dd/yy. We should add locale hints in prompts as temporary mitigation.

jordan: Newmark will accept a soft route fallback: route="date-normalize" -> serve merged-int8 (not quantized) for 48h canary while we ship fix. They asked for cost delta numbers though.

lee: Cost delta rough calc: int8 route ~ +0.22 cents/1000 tokens vs int4, but reduces error rate from 18% -> 5% on date cases. I'll add precise per-token cost delta to the ticket.

anika: Full eval finished: final F1 0.91 for token-bypass + small lora_alpha tweak. Hallucination (wrong date) 1.2% vs baseline 0.4%. Not perfect but acceptable for canary. Artifacts uploaded: https://tickets.internal/ML-2440 and s3://redwood-evals/newmark/1812345670/results.jsonl

jordan: OK let's do route-level canary to int8 for date-normalize route and enable token-bypass patch in staging. Lee can you draft the canary steps and rollback criteria?

lee: Drafting now: 1) create route rule for date-normalize to prefer newmark/merged-int8 2) deploy 5% of production traffic for 24h 3) monitor F1 and latency; if F1 < 0.9 or latency increase > 50ms rollback. Will attach runbook.

anika: I'll prepare a follow-up PR to include a prompt-level locale hint and a tokenizer-compat test in our merge CI to prevent regressions.

jordan: Thanks team. I'll notify Newmark AE + CS with canary plan. Please keep exec summary short for them (include cost delta).

(End of thread)
